texts: Longer endowment histories were hitting an RPC query limit. The console now reads logs by endowment address and decodes the events locally. That keeps gifts, patrons and activity readable as the history grows, without the old multi-event query restriction.

A payment receipt can exist before the RPC is ready to return it. Bursar's Base intake now retries missing receipts within its wait window instead of stopping at the first lookup error. No receipt still means unconfirmed, never an assumed payment.

We added a card-funding route for agent endowments. A Coinbase purchase sends USDC on Base through Relay, which delivers USDG to the endowment on Robinhood Chain. The giver needs no onchain signature or gas. Coinbase login and fees still apply.

Over the limit, the contract reverts it. Fund it once with stocks. The agent spends the draw. Open source. Grabbing some coffee, an

Three seconds after the payment settled, the sale landed in the agent's endowment on Robinhood Chain: half joined the principal, half went to the mandate the agent spen

An agent that earns can now grow its own endowment on Bursar. Our demo agent on Base sells a market note for half a cent. We paid it from a plain wallet on Base with the standard x402 client. Three seconds after the payment settled, the sale landed in the agent's endowment on Robinhood Chain: half j

When an AI agent pays for work, both sides need a way to contest the outcome without deciding the payout themselves. Bursar links each job to USDG escrow, a deadline and an onchain dispute process on Robinhood Chain. A $BURSAR thread 🧵

Too few votes do not hand the payer an automatic win. The escrow reopens with more time for delivery, and the dispute bond returns. A second dispute cannot freeze that lock again. If it remains locked past its deadline, a refund can be claimed.

One limit worth knowing before you integrate. A dispute after payout can affect the provider's reputation, but cannot pull back funds already paid. The safeguards depend on when a dispute is raised, and on the resolver roster and voting configuration.

What actually stops an agent from overspending? Each Bursar mandate is its own account on chain: per call, per day, per month, which providers, and when you sign off. Payment rides the x402 retry and sits in escrow for one job. New providers start capped at 25 USDG. Live on @RobinhoodApp Chain.

ordewell_ai.bio: One planner. Multiple AI agents. Parallel coding, smarter workflows, full control.
texts: Ordewell in one screen: Terminal: npx ordewell VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf: the Ordewell extension You need: one coding agent, Node 20.3+, git Free and open source, Apache 2.0. Read the plan before you pay for it.
GitHub: https://github.com/ordewell/ordewell Docs: https://ordewell.ai/docs

New in Ordewell 0.11: check-and-fix loops. A check runs. While it fails, the fix runs on the latest landed work, then the check runs again. Three rounds by default, ten at most, no planner turn in between. npm install -g ordewell@latest
Also in 0.11: research tasks that wake the planner with their report, account limits in the footer, and compaction that pauses instead of failing. https://ordewell.ai/news

Hit your 5-hour limit mid-run? In Ordewell the task pauses instead of failing. Claude Code and Codex name the reset, and the task picks up in its saved session. Or move it to another agent and the unfinished work comes along. Your account's own limits sit in the footer.

Most orchestrators start by asking for an API key. Ordewell can plan with the coding agent you're already signed into: Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode. It runs read only, and Ordewell never reads or stores your credential. Prefer a key? 25 providers work too.

How Ordewell works. 01 Say what you want. It reads your repo and asks. 02 Shape the plan. Change any task, agent or model. 03 Read the diff, then merge. Every change task works on its own branch. Yours waits for you.
Burned Supply! https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/tx/0x82abeaa37266dd38c3130cbd1d719b97e8af94253f6e68903ff18a7fb4d45776

A security refactor and a README update don't need the same model. In Ordewell each task picks its own runner, model and effort: - Claude Code for the audit - Codex for the refactor - OpenCode with a budget model for docs One plan. Move any task to another agent.

Agents are bad at grading themselves. So in Ordewell a task passes only when its agent calls task_complete on Ordewell's own tool server. No report means fail, even if the session exited cleanly. No second model is asked whether it looks done.

Every task in an Ordewell plan names its agent, model and effort before anything runs. Swap a model. Rewire a dependency. Drop a task. A bad plan you can edit costs a minute. A bad plan that already ran costs an afternoon.

Five agent tabs open. One is waiting for approval. One says "all done!" but never compiled. One has been idle for 14 minutes. You've become the scheduler. Ordewell gives you one planner instead. It reads your repo, asks what's unclear, then writes the plan.

sborindex.name: SBOR · Standard Bitcoin Offered Rate
sborindex.bio: The daily reference rate for borrowing dollars against bitcoin. Read from lending contracts, posted on-chain. Free to read, built for agents.
texts: Before an agent borrows, it can ask one question: is this rate fair? SBOR's MCP server answers with the gap to the market rate in basis points, and tells the agent to stop when an offer is more than 50 bps above it. Free, no key, no sign-up.

After each daily fixing, SBOR posts the day's rates to contracts on Stacks, Arc, Base, Hyperliquid and Solana. Any app, vault or agent can read them on-chain, and anyone can check a past day against what was posted that day. https://sbor.xyz/?v=3

Your agent is borrowing blind. Thursday, November 5, 6 PM ET: a 45 minute @BFFARMY_ session. Connect an agent to SBOR and it checks any loan offer against the market rate before it borrows. Free. No key, no signup, no wallet. https://x.com/BFFARMY_/status/2115518042562072816

A benchmark that always has an answer is sometimes guessing. When SBOR can't read enough of a rate's markets, it withholds the rate and says why. A missing number means unknown, never zero. The rules behind every fixing: https://sbor.xyz/paper.html

60 days of SBOR. A fixing every morning since September 1, none missed, weekends included. Every one read from the lending contracts, every market shown, never rewritten. A benchmark is earned one fixing at a time. https://sbor.xyz/?v=3

Borrowing dollars against bitcoin cost 5.45% in this morning's fixing, down from 6.00% a day earlier. The largest market, USDC against cbBTC on Morpho on Base, went from 6.26% to 5.71%. Every market behind it at https://sbor.xyz/?v=3

5% and 5% are not always the same rate. Protocols quote on different bases, and a nominal 5% compounded continuously costs 5.13% over a year. SBOR converts each market's rate to one effective annual basis before it averages them. https://sbor.xyz

Borrowing dollars against bitcoin cost 6.00% in this morning's fixing, up from 5.10% a day earlier. The largest market, USDC against cbBTC on Morpho on Base, went from 5.30% to 6.26%. Every market behind it at SBOR.

The SBOR white paper is out. What a reference rate for loans against bitcoin must be, how SBOR computes it, and what changes when lenders and borrowers use the same rate. Stamped on Bitcoin, Arc, Base, Hyperliquid, Solana and Stacks. https://sbor.xyz/whitepaper

Check it yourself. The PDF's SHA-256 is eb87f320b33ff590a6bab498167ee2d192525f7c3edc28604a2af13a66cfe638, posted on all six chains on 25 October. The page checks the file in your browser and links every transaction.

Every lending pool has two prices: what borrowers pay and what lenders earn. Lenders earn less, because only part of the pool is lent out and the protocol keeps a share. That is why SBOR publishes two rates, a borrow rate and a supply rate, every day. https://sbor.xyz

What a dollar costs, 21 Oct. Rate, then utilization. Stacks, SBOR-USD, against crypto collateral: 2.83%, 56.92% Against plain bitcoin, BTC-COLLATERAL-USD, 19 markets on 5 chains: 5.08%, 89.71% Against US Treasuries, SOFR (19 Oct): 3.87%

An app shows you a rate. The lending contract is what charges it. SBOR reads its rates from the contracts' own state every morning, and lists every market behind each number on the site, so anyone can check the source. https://sbor.xyz
SBOR-BTC, 20 Oct fixing: borrow 1.50%, supply 1.34%. 19 Oct: 1.30% and 0.81%. Its one market, sBTC on Zest, went from 70.62% to 99.97% utilization over the same two fixings.
First stablecoin sub-rate: borrowing RLUSD against bitcoin costs 3.70% today (BTC-COLLATERAL-RLUSD), beside 5.06% for USDC. One rate per stablecoin once $25M of it is weighted in.
PoX cycle 144 paid 7.859 BTC to STX stakers, up 58.9% on cycle 143, with 448.3M STX locked, up 1.5%. Every cycle, read from the chain, formula shown: https://sbor.xyz

What does it cost to borrow dollars against bitcoin? SBOR reads the lending contracts every morning and publishes one dated rate. 16 October: 5.10% to borrow, across 20 markets on 6 chains and $3.1B supplied. Every market behind it is shown. https://sbor.xyz
The same bitcoin, borrowed in different dollars. 16 October: 5.23% in USDC on Base, 2.99% in USDT on Ethereum, 1.79% in USD1 on BNB Chain. One reference rate puts them side by side.

Built for AI agents. Before your agent borrows, it can check the offer against SBOR. Free MCP server, no key: npx -y sbor-mcp. Each day’s rate is also posted on-chain on Arc, Base, Hyperliquid, Solana and Stacks.

Is 6% a good rate to borrow dollars against bitcoin? Alone, a rate tells you nothing. Credit markets judge offers against a published market rate, like SOFR for dollars borrowed against Treasuries. SBOR publishes one for dollars borrowed against bitcoin. https://sbor.xyz

protocol_v4.bio: The v4 aggregator that leaves no trail. Best split across every pool, hooks included, sent to a fresh shadow. Routes for agents over x402.
texts: Four days, six more things live, and every one started with someone hitting a wall during a real swap: hooks that price by gas, a wallet reading a stale node, a balance that didn’t show. Now the router quotes at your real gas price, checks your wallet’s connection before you sign, and hands you a re

A swap can be fine on chain and still fail in your wallet, simply because the wallet is reading the chain through a node that fell behind. That’s why the router asks both before it lets you sign, and if your wallet is the problem, it fixes the connection for you. https://www.protocolv4.xyz/swap CA:

No token list to wait for, no listing to request. Paste a contract address and the router works out where it actually trades and the best way to reach it. A fresh launch and a deep pool take the same three steps. $PV4

Every swap from your main wallet adds to a public history anyone can read. Shadow addresses give you fresh ones, rebuilt from one free signature every time you need them. No key file to lose, no database of yours on our servers.

Wrapping ETH was always a tax: an extra step, an extra approval, extra gas, and WETH left behind when something fails halfway. In v4 a pool can hold ETH itself, and when it does the router pays it in directly. Your ETH goes in, your token comes out.

A quote taken at zero gas price looks great and fails on chain, because some v4 hooks set their fee from the transaction’s own gas price. We learned that from a real reverted swap, and fixed it the same day: every quote, preflight and floor is now simulated at the base fee you’ll actually pay. https

Plenty of tokens launch with a deck and a “coming soon”. $PV4 launched with a router you can use right now, and it gets better every week from what people run into while using it. Open it, swap something small, judge for yourself.

A success screen is easy to fake. A block isn’t. When your swap lands, the router reads what actually hit your wallet and what the network charged, straight from the chain, and puts it next to the price you were quoted. Trust the receipt, not the app.

The safest money is money that never leaves your hands. There’s no Protocol V4 balance to top up and no vault to trust: your tokens leave your wallet, go through the pools, and come back to it, all inside one transaction you sign yourself. https://www.protocolv4.xyz/swap

Doing a good swap by hand means knowing which pools exist, what each one keeps, whether the token is still on its curve, and how to cut your size between them, all before the price moves. We turned that whole afternoon into a quote you can read in five seconds.

Uniswap v4 spread liquidity across more pools than anyone can watch: every fee tier, every hook, every launch curve. You shouldn’t have to pick. Tell the router what you want and how much, it finds the pools and fills them all in the same transaction. $PV4

Update: swap receipts. A quote is a promise. A receipt is proof. After every swap, the router now reads the block it landed in and tells you what really reached your wallet, how that compares to what you were quoted, and what the gas cost you. And if your wallet doesn’t list the token yet, one click

Pools named, hooks named, fee per leg, minimum per leg, the block it was priced at, the link the moment it’s sent. If you like to know exactly what you signed, this router was built for you. $PV4 https://www.protocolv4.xyz/swap
Every fix this week started as a reply under one of our posts. Keep them coming: tell us what confused you, what was slow, what didn’t work. We read all of it, and the router is better for it.

On this chain the network fee is so low that the trade itself is all that matters. Which is exactly why routing matters: the difference between a good and a bad route is worth far more than the gas you’ll ever pay here. https://www.protocolv4.xyz/swap
Never used a v4 router? Bring a small amount, keep some ETH aside for gas, and read the route before you sign. The page checks the rest and won’t let you send a swap that would fail.

Comparing a quote to a chart is comparing a crowd to one person. The chart shows the last trade. Your quote shows what your exact size gets after it pushes through every pool on the route, fees and depth included. The router shows both, so you can see the gap before you sign.

Anyone can spin up a thousand AI judges. If ruling cost nothing, one person could fill the court with their own. So on GenLayer, every validator has to lock GEN before it gets a vote.

Appeal a verdict and the jury can grow, so controlling the outcome requires influencing more validators. And a validator caught cheating loses part of what it locked. Full GEN tokenomics: https://portal.genlayer.foundation/genesis/tokenomics

texts: Traditional finance has dark pools for a reason: when large orders are visible, the market moves against them. Onchain agents don’t have an equivalent yet. That’s the gap we’re building for.
Things NOCTIS will never ask you for: your seed phrase, a DM to “help” you buy, a “verification” transaction, or payment to join a whitelist. If someone asks, it isn’t us.
Most “AI agent” tokens are a chatbot with a wallet. The hard part isn’t the AI. It’s letting it act with real money safely, privately and within limits.
One of the hard parts we’re working through: running an LLM inside an enclave. Models are large, enclave memory is limited, and confidential GPUs cost more. We’ll share how we handle each one.
We’re designing NOCTIS as an execution layer, not another agent. Bring your own agent, any model or framework. We handle where it runs and how its trades settle.
Who NOCTIS is for: builders who don’t want their agent cloned the day it works, desks that don’t want to broadcast positions, and anyone letting an agent manage money without exposing their wallet.

What NOCTIS doesn’t hide: that a trade happened, enclave attestations, your policy hash, our contract code. What it does hide: your strategy, which trades are yours, your wallet, your exact rules. Private isn’t invisible.

What happens if someone tricks your agent with a malicious prompt or a fake data feed? On NOCTIS, the worst case is a rejected transaction. The contract checks where funds go and how much, whatever the agent says.
A sandwich attack, explained: a bot sees your buy, buys first, lets you buy at the higher price, then sells. Its profit is the extra you paid. It only works because your order was visible.
A human trader makes a few trades a day. An AI agent can trade all day, every day. Every trade is another clue about the strategy. Agents need privacy more than people do.
Honest question for anyone running a trading bot onchain: have you ever checked how easy it is to trace your bot’s wallet back to you?
“Why not just use a private RPC?” A private RPC hides one order from the mempool. It doesn’t hide your strategy, your wallet, or your trade history. The agent is still an open book.
The better your onchain agent performs, the faster it gets copied. Copy-trading bots scan for winning wallets all day. On a public chain, success is a signal. $NOCTIS
Your agent trades. Nobody watches. NOCTIS is live on Robinhood Chain. Your strategy is sealed in your browser, then the runner trades it on Uniswap within limits enforced on chain. $NOCTIS
Dex paid. $NOCTIS token info, socials and website are now live on DexScreener.

Website is live. Architecture, contracts, and roadmap for NOCTIS: private execution for AI agents. https://usenoctis.xyz
What is NOCTIS? A private execution layer for AI agents that trade onchain. Your agent’s strategy, orders, and wallet stay private. A thread on what we’re building and how it works.
Safety by design Hard limits (max size, allowed assets, weekly cap) are enforced by the vault contract onchain. Even if the model makes a bad call, it can’t move funds outside the rules you set.

texts: Same app, real privacy. Until this week Meryal's withdrawals were checked in the open. Now the contract only sees a Groth16 proof: no note, no index, no trace of the deposit it came from. Try it with a few dollars. https://www.meryalraven.sbs/spend

Your note never leaves your browser. Meryal's prover runs locally: snarkjs, the circuit's wasm and its key, served as plain files. It builds the witness from your seed and hands the relayer a proof and the public inputs, nothing else.

Update: No single key can read a Meryal position anymore. Sealed notes are encrypted to a key split in three. Two shares open a note, and the contract only accepts them near its liquidation price. Each keeper bonds $MERY. Deposits are approved on chain; only a multisig can refuse one.
Good morning team

Privacy only wins when it is the cheap default. On Meryal it already costs the user nothing extra: the proof takes two seconds in your browser, the relayer pays the gas, and the address that receives the money has never been seen before.

A public chain is a public diary. Every wallet you use can be read: what you hold, what you borrowed, where you spent it. Meryal breaks the thread between the position and the spending, with a proof instead of a promise. CA 0x134e52ed8Ee01Cbb1FB714098B606C57366369Fd

Need cash without selling your NVDA? Borrow against it at the Morpho market's rate. The USDG arrives as private notes, and you spend them from addresses nobody can tie to your position. Unaudited beta, small amounts. https://www.meryalraven.sbs/borrow

Tokenized stocks now have a five-year path to trade on chain. On chain, every position is readable: size, debt, liquidation price, and the wallet behind it. Meryal's sealed positions keep all of that behind a commitment, and prove on every step that the loan stays safe.

Shielded pools are turning into the privacy layer for payments. Meryal plugs a credit source into one: borrow against a stock token and the USDG lands in the pool as notes, withdrawn later by a zero-knowledge proof to any address. Shares in, private cash out.

Sealed positions are live on Meryal. Deposit NVDA, borrow USDG, repay, withdraw: each change is a proof made in your browser. The chain records a commitment and the amounts that moved, not whose position it is or how big it has grown.

Major Update live now : Meryal's privacy is now zero-knowledge. Withdrawals, credit activations and sealed positions are Groth16 proofs made in your browser in two seconds. A sealed position hides its size and debt, yet proves it stays solvent at every step. http://www.meryalraven.sbs/sealed CA: 0x1

Every credit line has an end date. After expiry and a grace hour anyone can close it, and what the agent did not spend goes back into the pool as the owner's note. The caller cannot send it anywhere else.

No IOU on Meryal is unsecured. When a line is reserved, the vault borrows its whole limit into escrow against the owner's stock. Every IOU is paid from that escrow, and the vault's liquidation rules keep the borrow solvent.

A finished session still holds dust. A one-time address holds a payment. Neither needs gas to clean up. The address signs once, the recycler deposits the rest into the pool, and the nonce fixes the note and the fee so a relayer can change neither.

x402 with a stealth extension. The agent signs a ReceiveWithAuthorization made out to Meryal's settler, with a nonce that commits to the one-time address. Whoever submits it, the USDG can only land there, announced once.

Agents paying agents means every agent is also a merchant. On Meryal a merchant publishes one meta-address. Each x402 payment to it lands at a new one-time address, settled by a contract that can only send it there. Revenue that is not a public line.

Every x402 payment is a public receipt: who paid whom, how much, when. Run an agent from one wallet and its whole shopping list is on chain. On Meryal each session pays from a fresh address, and a merchant with a meta-address is paid at a new one-time address every time.
Good morning

An agent never keeps the same address for long. A session lasts until it is spent, an hour old or 20 payments in, by default. Then the issuer derives the next one and moves on. Watch any one address and you see a short session, not the agent.

texts: Privacy is not a single feature. It is a sequence of verifiable properties. 🌘 Eclipse now presents its privacy model layer by layer, showing what remains visible, what becomes hidden and where trust assumptions still exist. The roadmap progresses through: • Batch Actions Individual swaps are combine

Different markets require different liquidity routes. They should not require different execution guarantees. 🌘 The Eclipse market layer currently demonstrates three execution environments: • WETH/USDG through the Uniswap v4 EclipseHook • NVDA/USDG through a 24/7 tokenized-equity route • PONS/USDG t

Dark Waves are running on the Eclipse. Every 30 seconds, Eclipse collects orders into a single wave. Inside each wave: • Compatible buy and sell orders are matched internally • A uniform clearing price is calculated • Only the remaining imbalance is routed through the Uniswap v4 Hook • The completed

Privacy should be explained, not implied. 🌘 Eclipse shows exactly what becomes visible at every stage of the protocol. A standard public DEX swap can reveal: • The trader’s wallet • Token direction • Order size • Minimum output • Information that searchers may use before execution Eclipse Dark Mode
The goal: prove that the wave followed the protocol’s rules without exposing every individual order publicly. Private execution. Verifiable settlement. Public liquidity.

Eclipse’s zero-knowledge circuit prover is running. 🌘 The Rust zkVM verifies each Dark Wave before settlement: • No duplicate order IDs • Order deadlines remain valid • Private orders are included in the commitment root • Internal crossing uses the correct clearing price • Gross volume equals matche

Why does it matter? • Less individual order-flow exposure • Internal matching can reduce volume hitting the public pool • Lower potential market impact • Existing Uniswap v4 liquidity remains accessible • Minimum-received and slippage protection • Onchain status and transaction records Private execu

What happens when you choose Dark Mode on Eclipse? 🌘 Instead of executing as a separate public swap, your order is escrowed onchain and joins the next 30–60 second Eclipse Wave. Set the line before you leave. Choose the balance you want to keep. When your account drops below it, your agents pause themselves instead of burning through what is left. https://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/f1bfbdec8aeb52a9ac0d4a2d12d51cf1ec0c64ce

If an agent is doing the same approved task for the next hour, you should not have to approve every single request. Approve it once for the hour. Your other limits still apply, and you can end the approval early whenever you want. http://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/d9

The fastest way through the product is often the keyboard. Press `?` on any page to see the shortcuts available there, with the right keys for Mac or PC. https://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/46d66fee21704ea3e92ea0cb15f23e901f925e32

Your agent can be stopped from your phone too. In your linked Telegram chat, type `/stop Shop bot 1h` to pause it for an hour. Use `/start Shop bot` when you are ready to start it again. https://anyroute.tech/docs/#telegram-stop

The full model catalogue is useful. Your own usage is more useful. Filter it to the models you have actually called, then see your spend and success rate for each one. https://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/bd354dffde1b520ce1d2d393562c682d65e3ed36
A long chat can quietly add up. Set a spending cap on a chat. A send that would go over it is held, so you can raise the cap or send anyway. https://anyroute.tech/docs/#chat-cap

A useful answer should not disappear into a long chat. Pin any message to the top, then jump back to it whenever you need it. https://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/88c76a301623e76ce6e34af9d69d064c743ef975

Some of the quieter work has been landing too: 1. Pin important messages in long chats 2. See the models you actually use, with spend and success rate 3. Press ? to see shortcuts for the page you are on More updates will be up soon. https://anyroute.tech

Your agent does not need access around the clock. Set its working days, hours, and time zone in Agents. Outside that window, it either blocks the request or sends it to you for approval. https://anyroute.tech/docs/#work-hours

A request gets blocked. Instead of guessing, Anyroute tells you why. Every refusal links to the rule behind it and the exact setting you need to change. https://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/e4ec5ddc8d2a6ad13cd299cbd6c17a60b9324d3b

When something is not working, it helps to know whether it is your setup or ours. Turn on incident alerts in Settings and get a notice when an issue opens, is updated, and is resolved, in your Inbox or Telegram. They are off by default. https://anyroute.tech/docs/#incident-alerts

Before changing an agent’s rules, you should know what that change will actually do. Anyroute shows the difference in plain words and replays it against last week’s calls before you save anything. https://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/99988f202073b8317576cf9eb91f5aa06db

You may be paying more than you need to for work a similar model can handle. Ways to save compares your last 30 days of usage with similar models and shows the estimated difference. Try one in Chat before you change anything. https://anyroute.tech/docs/#savings-finder

A quick view of your account, without opening the dashboard. Choose a daily or weekly summary of your agents, spend, and models, then pick when it arrives. https://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/6e3466aa30acb434a89deffd99470d243eba92c3

When a model you rely on goes down, refreshing its page is not a plan. Watch it once and Anyroute lets you know when it becomes unavailable, then when it is back, in your Inbox or on Telegram. https://anyroute.tech/docs/#model-watch

Some things need your attention, just not right now. Snooze an Inbox notice for an hour, until tomorrow, or until Monday. It comes back unread at the time you chose. https://anyroute.tech https://github.com/AnyRouteRH/AnyRoute/commit/78392ea59c58cd18328a86d16c03d507604af189

现象：字幕用 data-subs 属性传 JSON 字符串，页面渲染出来内容被拦腰截断，还不报错。 误判：一开始怀疑是数据没传全，或者 JSON 格式本身有问题，查了半天。 根因：转义函数没处理双引号，JSON 里的 " 直接把 HTML 属性值提前截断，解析器读到一半就停了，静默失败，压根不会报错。 判据：往 HTML 属性里塞 JSON/富文本，双引号不转义就是定时炸弹——它不报错，只是悄悄丢内容。 #前端踩坑

给审核模块接上事实源后，开始报一堆假阳性——本该核对数字的逻辑，把写法判据也当数字去核对，一堆「没出处」的误报。 我一开始以为是提示词不够精确，想着再加约束描述。 查到根因：facts和playbook被塞进了同一个数组返回。facts是带出处的数字事实，playbook是写法规则，压根没有数字可核对。结构长得一样，下游拿同一套逻辑处理，误判是必然的。 判据：校验语义不同的数据，哪怕字段结构一样，也别塞进同一个数组——下游只认结构，不认语义。 #系统设计

alloomiai.bio: Self-evolving digital employees for professional services.
texts: An AI employee should learn the method, not copy yesterday's answer. Our bar for Alloomi: expert feedback must transfer to a new matter with changed facts—without importing the previous client's terms. Test the next decision, not just recall of the last one.

One approved exception must not become an AI employee's standing rule. At Alloomi, our context design keeps the source, scope and validity of a decision. The test: reuse the right lesson on the next task without turning a one-off approval into a permanent policy.

An AI employee's memory should preserve professional judgment—not just past conversations. At Alloomi, we design context around the work: what applies now, where it came from, and who can use it. Corrections update the working state without erasing its history.

The hardest context isn't in the document. It's the old detail the user didn't know to retrieve. Our design principle: assemble context around the decision, not just the latest file. That means: → Recall across documents and conversations. → Keep source, time and scope attached. → Separate evidence

A self-evolving agent can compound expertise—or compound error. The difference is safeguards. Real-world feedback is noisy, contradictory, and sometimes adversarial. Letting every successful-looking trajectory become training data is not learning. It is an uncontrolled feedback loop. Our safeguards

Most agents can finish a task. The harder question is whether run 100 is better than run 1. Alloomi filters and replays feedback from real work for post-training, anchors learning to expert standards, and carries that experience into the next delivery.
An agent that remembers across tools is useful. An agent that remembers the wrong version across tools is worse. Durable memory needs provenance, freshness, and correction—not just consolidation.

Self-reflection has a ceiling: the model is still grading itself with the judgment it already has. It can catch an inconsistency or rewrite a weak answer. But another reasoning pass cannot teach the model why an expert rejected a clause, changed a recommendation, or approved an exception. Our learni

Worktrees isolate code. They don't keep agents aligned. Give every agent its own worktree and the real failure mode remains: one thread changes the plan while another keeps coding against the old decision. The branches are isolated. The shared understanding isn't. That's not a Git problem. It's a co

The next phase of AI agents won't be decided by how smart the model is. Every frontier model is brilliant out of the box — and identical for everyone. What nobody can copy is the judgment an agent absorbed inside YOUR business. Intelligence is where every agent begins. Experience is where they diver

OpenContext holds 67% on BEAM at 10M tokens. RAG collapses to 24.9%, and the best published system to 26.6%. Your agent forgets why it made decisions. OpenContext fixes that. Holistic context with temporal timelines, belief revision, and experience that compounds into context instead of resetting. C

A 1M-token context window is not memory. It is a larger desk. It can hold more history, but it still cannot tell an agent which facts are current, which have expired, or which only apply to one customer. Holistic Context assigns each memory a scope across task, conversation, channel, person, and val

Here's our bet: agents should learn from the work itself. Not context sitting in a database — experience written back into the model's weights. Every task finished → data earned. Every judgment captured → next delivery better. The work makes the agent better. The better agent makes better work.

Agreed. But most compilers still retrieve-then-forget. Context is a scratchpad, RAG is the default. Ask, pull, answer, drop it. That's a nicer filing cabinet, not compilation. Real compilation starts from a context that never turns off. Tracked, checked against itself, learning as it goes what's wor

The most valuable training data for an agent can't be scraped off the internet. It's the stuff that lives in one person's head: why that revision happened, what "good" actually looks like, which customer means what. Private. Dynamic. Produced only through real work. This is exactly where a general-p

Every developer's trying to fix "agents don't learn" the same three ways: → Wrappers — connect tools, but the model underneath stays frozen → RAG — more facts, but never the judgment behind a decision → Fine-tuning — slow, expensive, always a step behind the business All three hand the agent more in

Everyone's racing to make AI agents smarter — bigger models, longer context, more tools. But nobody says the uncomfortable part out loud: for most agents, the 100th time doing a task is no different from the first. Humans compound through reps. Agents reset every time. That's not a model problem. It

Computer use is a breakthrough. But clicking faster does not make AI a better lawyer. The gap is judgment. Alloomi: → builds temporal matter context from meetings, emails, prior drafts, client preferences, and precedents → completes the review and redline, escalating judgment calls for approval → tu

texts: arclUSDC is not being designed as “another stablecoin.” The idea is a productive USDC layer. Deposit USDC. Receive arclUSDC. Let underlying strategies generate yield. Then make that capital composable with the rest of Arclight. Yield should be a primitive, not a destination.

One overlooked benefit of concentrated liquidity ladders: you can encode a strategy into the shape of the liquidity itself. More capital near spot. More capital above. More capital below. One-sided exits. Bid/ask structures. Arclight turns those choices into up to 32 V3/V4 positions in one transacti

Arclight positions are not black boxes. The builders are onchain. The staking contract is onchain. The LP NFTs sit in the user’s wallet. The usage numbers can be independently checked. We want the homepage to show the metrics. We want the contracts to prove them.

The most interesting part of the @arcloak integration is not that Arclight processes a payment. It is that Arcloak does not need to become a payments company to offer paid inference. They build the product. Arclight handles x402 verification, settlement and gas sponsorship underneath. That is exactl

You can now look at Arclight adoption from two different angles. Liquidity side: hundreds of LP positions created through the builders. Payments side: millions of $ARCLIGHT locked to unlock x402 seller capacity. Two completely different products. One protocol starting to develop usage on both sides.

Arclight’s x402 facilitator is designed around one simple rule: the buyer should do as little as possible. Hold USDC or EURC. Sign once. Done. No API key. No pre-funding account. No native gas balance. The complexity belongs in the infrastructure, not in the user flow.

A good LP builder should tell you when not to build. That is why we are integrating @arc_vein pool grades and impostor detection directly into Arclight. If a pool is E-graded or the “USDC” is not really USDC, the warning should happen before the signature. Safety belongs in the execution flow.

Arclight’s edge is not one feature. It is the fact that the same stack can help you: find liquidity grade the risk build the position track the result move value through x402 and eventually keep idle USDC productive through arclUSDC That is a much bigger surface area than a simple LP interface.

Arclight is not trying to be “another LP dashboard.” The stack is becoming much broader: precision V3/V4 liquidity deployment live x402 settlement infrastructure NEAR account payments seller staking risk-aware pool discovery arclUSDC on the roadmap cross-chain funding via NEAR Intents Liquidity is t

arclUSDC is where the wider Arclight thesis gets interesting. The plan is simple: USDC enters. Yield is sourced underneath. arclUSDC represents the position. That productive capital can eventually plug back into liquidity and payment flows. Idle capital should not have to stay idle.

One of our favourite Arclight integrations is @arcloak. Their product can focus on inference while Arclight handles the x402 payment layer underneath: verification, gas sponsorship and settlement on @arc. That is what good infrastructure looks like. The end user sees the product, not the plumbing.

Arclight’s indexer is built as its own layer for a reason. Execution happens onchain. The indexer reconstructs positions, fees, swaps and realised returns. The frontend reads the resulting state. That separation lets us improve analytics without touching the contracts that actually move capital. Cle

The next phase of Arclight is about making the builder smarter before you even sign. Through the @arc_vein integration, pool grades and impostor-token warnings can be surfaced directly inside the build flow. Better execution matters. Avoiding the wrong pool matters even more.

LP discovery should tell you more than TVL. Arclight Pools now surfaces metrics like VOL/TVL so you can see not just how much liquidity is sitting in a pool, but how hard that capital is actually working. A large pool is not automatically an efficient one.

$ARCLIGHT utility is tied directly to infrastructure usage. Sellers stake for more gas-sponsored x402 throughput: 250K → 500 settles/day 1M → 1,500/day 5M → no per-seller cap Buyers never need the token. Usage on one side. Frictionless payments on the other.

The Arclight x402 facilitator has moved well beyond a proof of concept. USDC + EURC settlement. Gas sponsorship. Resource discovery. NEAR account payments. Seller staking tiers. Arc USDC support merged upstream. The boring payment plumbing is becoming real infrastructure.

One architectural decision we care about: Arclight does not need to custody your LP position to manage the build. The builder orchestrates the transaction, the position is created, and the LP NFT lands directly in your wallet. Infrastructure should reduce complexity without taking ownership away fro

Arclight is being built for people who want sophisticated LP execution without turning every position into a manual operation. Choose the pool. Set the range. Shape the liquidity. Split it across up to 32 rungs. Deploy the whole structure in one transaction. V3/V4 underneath. Much simpler on top.

Arclight is what happens when LP tooling stops treating users like protocol engineers. Pick the market. Shape the range. Split capital across multiple positions. Deploy. Track fees, PnL and realised returns. Underneath, it’s still Uniswap V3/V4 complexity. On the surface, it feels like one product.

The bigger Arclight thesis is starting to come into focus. Liquidity is where capital gets deployed. x402 is how machines spend it. arclUSDC is how idle capital earns. @NEARProtocol integration is how users come in from outside Arc. The opportunity is not one feature. It’s owning the capital flow be

texts: The first Cognia Cloud V4 update is live. You can now teach a Skill from a correction. Previously, creating a Skill meant writing it from scratch. Now, you can show Cognia what your agent got wrong, explain the correction, and provide the accepted result. Cognia drafts a private Skill for you to rev

Cognia Cloud V4 is ready, and the first update goes out today. This release brings a new way to turn corrections into reusable Skills, along with better routing, version controls, and comparisons to see what actually helps. We’re rolling it out in stages and sharing more about each update as it arri

Some of the most useful corrections happen in the middle of a task. Cloud V4 will bring new MCP tools for teaching and managing Skills, making it possible to turn those corrections into reusable guidance from a supported client.

Evidence helps users understand how a Skill performs in practice. With Cloud V4, we’re tightening how that evidence is counted. Internal tests and Skill comparisons won’t count toward usage, maturity, or rewards, keeping those results separate from real-world use.

How do you know whether a Skill is actually helping? In Cloud V4, you’ll be able to compare results with and without a Skill, or test two versions against each other. You can review the outputs without knowing which one produced them and see how they compare.

Cortex helps agents find useful Skills for the task at hand. In V4, we’re improving how it recognizes when a Skill is relevant. It will look beyond matching words to better understand the kind of work being requested, even when the task is phrased differently.

Teams often have their own way of doing things, and their agents need to follow the same guidance. Cloud V4 will let individuals and organizations choose which version of a Skill to use. If a revision isn’t working as expected, you’ll be able to return to an earlier version.

The way you want work done can change over time. Your Skills should be able to change with it. In Cloud V4, you’ll be able to revise a Skill with a new correction and keep its previous versions together, so you can see how it has changed.

A correction can contain details you don’t want passed around. In Cloud V4, the original material used to teach a Skill will stay private and won’t be automatically added to an agent’s context. The approved Skill can be used without sharing the original correction.

Creating a Cognia Skill has meant writing one from scratch. With Cloud V4, we’re making that process a little easier. You’ll be able to give Cognia a correction and turn it into a Skill for similar tasks. You can review and edit the draft before deciding whether to use it.

Each version of Cognia has brought us closer to making agents more useful over time. V1 introduced the memory network, giving agents a way to find and reuse knowledge. V2 made Cognia easier to use, with faster responses, better retrieval, simpler setup, and shared access for teams. V3 added The Reco
We’re still here, and we’re still building. We’ve been working on Cognia Cloud V4 and have more to share about what’s coming soon.
